### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /page — 1cr

Returns data from a Pillar page including display name, bio, avatar, and list of links with titles and URLs.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Pillar page

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/pillar/page?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## What Pillar is for

One endpoint, `/page` (1cr): a creator's Pillar page — their bio-link stack.

Same read as `linktree`: the links behind the bio, in the creator's own order, are the offer
ladder. Confirm from the handle's bio which host they use before calling — the five link-in-bio
platforms (`linktree`, `linkbio`, `linkme`, `komi`, `pillar`) each need their own endpoint.

> ⚠️ `prism/lookup` (0cr) does not resolve link-in-bio URLs — verified 07.10.26 in this
> workspace. Go straight to `/page`.
